In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient DC‐based vaccination strategy, which is able to induce strong and long‐lasting antigen‐specific CD8‐T‐cell immune responses.
the development of new vaccines based on the use of DC as antigen‐presenting cells.

the design of a novel and efficient vaccine strategy for the treatment of tumors and infectious diseases, based on antigen conjugation to the B subunit of CT and the subsequent uptake of the antigen–CT complex by DC.

the use of CT as an adjuvant and carrier for DC vaccination is highly efficient in inducing both humoral and cell‐mediated immune responses.

the use of CT in DC‐based vaccines is a promising strategy for the induction of CTL immune responses.

The main takeaway from our work is that
conjugating antigen to CT can enhance CTL responses and tumor immunity in vivo, even in the absence of adjuvants.
the use of CT‐conjugation of antigen for DC vaccination may provide a simple, effective and safe way to induce antigen‐specific CTL responses.
